title: frame
content_html:
frame

The titles frame (positive) and frame (negative) raise a question about what belongs to the work and what belongs to its surround. A crop, a border, a caption or a neighbouring image can change what counts as part of the subject. In doll cell [framed version], the frame adds a physical question about the relation between what is painted on the glass and what sits behind it. Frame (positive) · Doll cell [framed version]

Reading note. Existentialism. In “The Aesthetic Attitude,” Beauvoir examines what happens when someone approaches a situation as a detached spectator. A frame gives us a place to look from. What can we see from there, and which people or circumstances become easier to overlook? The Ethics of Ambiguity, part III, §1
